name: Routing review
question: Before routing: the layer roles, the power copper and how routing runs
why_now:
You asked for routing to start, with six outputs that perform the same and the lowest DCR, and for a review of KiCadRoutingTools (KRT) and ee-skills' `ee-layout-rules` first. Two read-only reviews, a resistance model of the board's planes and U401 fan-out trials found seven things to settle before any copper goes down. They depend on each other, D12-1 most of all. DEC-027 (PR #53) chose JLCPCB's JLC062012-1080 (1 oz outer, 2 oz inner) and left exactly these open: the layer roles, the outer copper and the via option.

Every number below can be re-run: the plane model is `placement/2026-11-02-bars/power/plane_model.py` (85 °C, all six outputs at 10 A unless stated). The fan-out trials are KRT's `bga_fanout.py` on the placed board.

facts.label: A channel's own resistance
facts.value: TPS2HCS08A on-resistance 8.9 mΩ typical at 25 °C, 17.8 mΩ max at 150 °C; channels may differ by up to 7 % (ΔRON). Copper differences well under that are not what makes one output worse

facts.label: What the fast routes got wrong (KRT review)
facts.value: Every 10 A output went out at 0.1 mm (OUT1–OUT6 were never given a power width); 3V3_MAIN was 465 tracks of 0.1 mm; the bulk step named the T1S trunk in --rip-existing-nets, which lifts route_diff's protection (16 of 82 mm coupled, 22 mm skew); route_open.sh's rip-anything-40-times laps caused the PHY/BGA churn. The fast routes were placement judges, not a routing method

facts.label: U401 escape on the chosen stackup
facts.value: JLCPCB allows 0.09/0.09 mm on the 1 oz outer layers and 0.15/0.15 mm on the 2 oz inner layers. Fan-out trials: F.Cu + B.Cu alone at 0.1/0.1 mm escape 55 of 55 signals with 0.45 mm vias; at 0.15/0.15 (2 oz outer) 54 of 55 (SWD_SWO) with 0.45 mm vias, 55 with 0.35/0.2 mm. The plan's "4 signal layers" count was wrong (it used the ball gap on every layer) and `escape_budget.py` now counts each layer's own channel

facts.label: Current per via
facts.value: IPC-2221's internal-conductor curve at JLCPCB's 18 µm plating gives 0.65 A per 0.45/0.25 mm via at a 10 °C rise, not the 1 A the placement plan assumed: 31 vias per switch's 20 A, 47 per FET pad's 30 A, 93 for the shunt's 60 A
facts.source: ee-layout-rules fab defaults (method); JLCPCB via stack on the fab page

facts.label: Rules ee-layout-rules adds with no decision needed
facts.value: Confine 0.1 mm track to scoped U401/U501 escape areas; no vias on the buck switch nodes; 1V5_CORE_FB 1 mm from either switch node; T1S pairs coupled (gap 0.15 ± 0.01 mm, ≤ 2 mm uncoupled, skew ≤ 0.5 mm) and 0.75 mm from other nets; switch nodes 10 mm from the T1S line; nothing but their own nets and GND under Y401/Y501; 0.3 mm PTH hole to copper; high-current pads solid to their pours; text 1.0 / 0.15 mm, mask web 0.10 mm; and prove every DRU rule fires on a copy before use. Net classes PWR_BATT, PWR_RAIL and SW_NODE with width floors follow D12-2

facts.label: Not adopted from ee-layout-rules
facts.value: Its 0.6/0.3 mm default via (Node60 keeps 0.45/0.25), 2 or 4 fiducials (D03 chose 3), light parts only on the bottom (Node60 reflows the bottom second), decaps on the IC's side (Node60 puts them on top, about 4 nH per loop, stated per rail), Tj ≤ 110 °C (the handbook's Tj(max) − 25 °C wins)

decisions.question: Which job does each inner layer do?
decisions.why_now: The layer next to the parts decides what every bottom-side net returns through: the T1S pair, both bucks, both crystals and the INA228 Kelvin lines all sit on B.Cu. The power planes decide the DCR of every output.

options.name: GND next to both outer layers, VBAT_PROT on In2 + In3
options.summary: In1 GND, In2 VBAT_PROT, In3 VBAT_PROT, In4 GND, as the fab page's stackup names them. Signals on F.Cu and B.Cu, which the fan-out trial shows is enough for U401; In2/In3 may carry short signal runs in windows away from the power path if routing needs them.
gains: Half the plane resistance of the other options, on both the supply and the return
Every outer layer sits on GND: the T1S pair, bucks and crystals included
Symmetric stackup, as quoted; no fab change
costs: Two routing layers for most of the board; the bottom is dense (280 parts), so routing is tighter
Signals crossing the board under the power path have only F and B

options.name: The placement plan: In1 GND, In2/In3 signal, In4 VBAT_PROT
options.summary: Four signal layers, one plane each for GND and VBAT_PROT.

measures.label: U401 escape
measures.value: 4 layers: 54 of 55 at 0.45 mm vias, 55 at 0.35

gains: The most routing room
costs: The T1S pair, bucks and crystals on B.Cu return through the 60 A battery plane
Twice the plane resistance of A

options.name: Swap: In1 VBAT_PROT, In2/In3 signal, In4 GND
options.summary: B with the planes swapped, so B.Cu sits on GND and F.Cu (decaps, J401, D201, C207/C217 only) on VBAT_PROT.

measures.label: U401 escape
measures.value: 4 layers: 54 of 55 at 0.45 mm vias, 55 at 0.35

gains: Four routing layers and GND under B.Cu
costs: Twice the plane resistance of A
In2 and In3 sit next to each other with no plane between: they need opposite directions (ee L-26)

recommendation.why: You asked for the lowest DCR: A halves every plane path and puts GND under both outer layers. U401 escapes on the outer layers alone, so the cost is routing room, which routing will tell; if B.Cu runs out, short In2/In3 windows away from the power path are the relief.

decisions.question: Outer copper: 1 oz as quoted, or 2 oz?
decisions.why_now: The handbook asks for 2 oz on high-current paths. With D12-1 A the big currents run in the 2 oz inner planes, but the six outputs (switch to header) and the power entry's pours are on the outer layers.

options.name: 1 oz outer, as quoted (DEC-027)
options.summary: Outputs as parallel pours on F.Cu and B.Cu with via arrays; the 0.09–0.1 mm escape stays.

measures.label: One output run, ~20 mm of a 6 mm pour on F + B

gains: No change to DEC-027 or the quote
Finest escape rules on the outer layers
costs: Output runs about twice the resistance of 2 oz

options.name: 2 oz outer
options.summary: A different JLCPCB stackup (amends DEC-027, needs a new quote); 0.15/0.15 mm on every layer.

measures.label: One output run, ~20 mm of a 6 mm pour on F + B
U401 escape
measures.value: 54 of 55 at 0.45 mm vias; 55 with the 0.20 mm via option

gains: Lowest DCR on the outputs and the power entry
Follows the handbook
costs: New stackup and quote; probably the 0.20 mm via option ($37.90 for 5) for U401

recommendation.why: On a channel of about 10–18 mΩ the output run is 1.0 against 0.5 mΩ, equal on all six; the quote, the stackup and the escape stay as they are. Take B if you want the last 5 % of DCR and accept a re-quote.

decisions.question: Re-compose the three output cells so all six outputs are identical?
decisions.why_now: The cells approved in D08 turn each switch 90°, so one output leaves south and the other north, and no switch is centred between its headers. Switch pins to header pin 1: OUT1 29.7, OUT2 21.2, OUT3 29.6, OUT4 21.3, OUT5 16.9, OUT6 27.6 mm.

options.name: Turn and centre every switch
options.summary: Each switch turned so its OUTa pins face its west header and OUTb its east one, centred between the two headers' pin 1 (x 77.65, 152.3, 226.9 mm), the cell's other parts re-placed round it the same way in all three. Every output becomes the same run: 18.65 mm sideways plus the same drop to the header row, as a mirrored pair of pours. A new block page (D13) shows it before it lands.

images.caption: Today's U601 cell (D08): OUT1 leaves south, OUT2 north

gains: Six identical output paths by construction
Shorter worst run (29.7 → about 20 mm)
costs: Replaces D08's three cells; the SNS/FLT parts and test points move with them

options.name: Keep the D08 cells
options.summary: Equalise in copper: lengthen or narrow the shorter runs to match the longest.
gains: No placement change
costs: Every output gets the worst output's resistance: the opposite of lowest DCR

recommendation.why: It is the only way to have six equal outputs without making five of them as bad as the sixth.

decisions.question: Balance the supply between the three switches?
decisions.why_now: Power enters on the left (J910, Q201/Q202, R201, Q203/Q204) and the switches run to the right, so with D12-1 A the supply plane is 0.17 / 0.34 / 0.44 mΩ to U601 / U701 / U801: a 0.27 mΩ spread, about 2 % of a channel and well under the switches' own 7 %.

options.name: Accept the spread
options.summary: Keep the power entry where it is; the spread is 2.7 mV at 10 A between the best and worst channel.
gains: No change to the power-entry block (D04)
costs: U801's channel about 2 % more drop than U601's

options.name: Feed VBAT_PROT at mid-board
options.summary: Move the disconnect FETs Q203/Q204 (and their gate drive) toward mid-board, so the planes are fed between U701 and the outer switches.
gains: Outer switches equal, all within 0.09 mΩ, and less loss
costs: Re-opens D04: the 60 A path from J910 to the FETs gets longer, and the HGATE drive runs further

options.name: A slot in the planes to force a mid feed (modelled, rejected)
options.summary: A 1 mm slot along y 95.5 mm, open only at x 150–165 mm.
gains: Outer switches equal
costs: Three times the resistance: the gap is a bottleneck

recommendation.why: With the planes of D12-1 A the spread is 2 % of a channel, a third of what the switches themselves may differ by; B buys equality by re-opening the power entry. If you want the outer two exactly equal, B is the way, not C.

decisions.question: The input shunt: one 0.25 mΩ, two in parallel, or a 4-terminal part?
decisions.why_now: All the node's current, up to 60 A, passes R201 (Stackpole CSS2725FTL250, 0.25 mΩ, 4 W, 0.9 W at 60 A). At 0.65 A per via its pads need about 93 vias to reach the planes, and its two pads are the narrowest point of the 60 A path. The LM74910H breaker and the INA228 are both set for 0.25 mΩ (DEC-001, DEC-002).

options.name: Keep one CSS2725FTL250
options.summary: Wide pours on both outer layers into its pads, the via arrays beside them.
gains: No change; settings stay
costs: One footprint carries 60 A; the via field around it crowds the Kelvin taps

options.name: Two 0.5 mΩ in parallel
options.summary: Same 0.25 mΩ, so the LM74910H and INA228 settings stay; 30 A and 0.45 W each, the current spread over two footprints.
gains: Half the current density at each pad
Settings unchanged
costs: The sense voltage must be averaged across the two (equal-length Kelvin taps through matching resistors), or the INA228 reads one shunt's share

options.name: One larger 4-terminal shunt
options.summary: Separate current and Kelvin terminals in a larger body (the parts record already looks for one; the library holds Isabellenhütte BVR/BVB and Vishay WSK1216 candidates). A part search sets the value; 0.2 or 0.3 mΩ means new LM74910H/INA228 settings.
gains: Best sense accuracy (true Kelvin)
Wider current terminals
costs: A part search, new library part, and recalculated breaker and INA228 settings

recommendation.why: It fixes the layout constraint and the sense accuracy at once, and the parts record already plans it; a parts session can search 4-terminal shunts and two-in-parallel 0.5 mΩ together, so you choose between B and C with real parts in front of you before the power entry is routed.

decisions.question: Count vias at 0.65 A each?
decisions.why_now: The gate's "room for vias at high-current pads" passed at 1 A per via, an assumption. IPC-2221 at JLCPCB's 18 µm plating gives 0.65 A at a 10 °C rise.

options.name: 0.65 A per 0.45/0.25 mm via
options.summary: Re-run the gate's via-room row at 0.65 A: 31 vias per switch's 20 A, 47 per FET pad, 93 for the shunt.
gains: A basis that can be checked
costs: Bigger via fields at the power pads

options.name: Keep 1 A and confirm in the thermal test
options.summary: Count at 1 A and let GATE-THM-02 prove it.
gains: Smaller via fields
costs: Risk found only on the bench

recommendation.why: It is the published method at the plating the fab states; the thermal test still confirms it.

decisions.question: How should routing run?
decisions.why_now: KRT routes signals well but doesn't size 10 A copper, ignores custom DRU rules and the crystal no-via rule, and churned at the PHY/BGA when allowed to rip anything. ee-layout-rules (L-69) says no unattended whole-board routing on the master.

options.name: Staged: power and critical nets by hand, KRT for the rest
options.summary: In order: (1) the new DRU rules, each proven to fire; (2) by hand and locked: the 60 A power entry, the six output cells' 10 A pours and via fields, both bucks' hot loops, the Kelvin nets, the T1S chain, U501's south edge and U401's 3V3 balls; (3) KRT: planes, U401/U501 fan-out (with --immovable-refs, never moving approved parts), the crystal on B.Cu, the remaining pairs; (4) KRT bulk route with power widths and the T1S never in --rip-existing-nets, laps limited to 5 rip-ups; (5) review: KiCad DRC with the board's own rules, KRT's review-routed-board, widths and via counts checked against IPC-2152, the six outputs' DCR re-measured from the copper. Every stage on a copy, each PR reviewed.
gains: Every high-current and critical path decided by a person and locked before the router runs
costs: Slower than one router pass

options.name: KRT end to end, then fix
options.summary: Route everything with KRT's pipeline and repair what review finds.
gains: Fast
costs: The 10 A copper and the T1S pair are what it handled worst

recommendation.why: The power copper you want equal and lowest-DCR is exactly what KRT can't size; the router is good at the 250 nets that remain.

answer: Reply with each decision and a letter, for example "D12-1 A, D12-2 A, D12-3 A, D12-4 A, D12-5 C, D12-6 A, D12-7 A", or a change to any. The no-decision rules in the facts above go in with D12-1.
sources: KRT routing review; ee-skills ee-layout-rules review (origin/main eded36c)
